title: Tries and Text-Based Data Structures
description: Tries, also known as prefix trees, are specialized tree-like data structures optimized for efficient retrieval of strings, making them ideal for autocomplete, spell-checking, and prefix-based searching. This module explores the structure and operations of tries, their advantages over other data structures like hash maps in string handling, and extends to related text data structures such as suffix trees and suffix arrays. You'll learn how to implement tries in JavaScript, perform insertions, searches, and deletions, and understand real-world applications in text processing.

lessons.title: Introduction to Tries
lessons.content: A trie is a tree-like data structure where each node represents a character of a string. Unlike binary trees, nodes in a trie can have multiple children, one for each possible character. Tries are especially useful for storing dictionaries or sets of strings where quick prefix-based search is needed. Key operations include insertion, search, and prefix matching.

lessons.title: Why Use Tries Instead of Hash Maps?
lessons.content: While hash maps provide O(1) average lookup, they do not handle prefix queries efficiently. Tries support prefix-based queries naturally, allowing operations like autocomplete or lexicographical ordering in O(k) time, where k is the length of the key. Tries also avoid collisions and hash function overhead.

lessons.content: Trie operations typically run in O(k) time, where k is the length of the key or prefix. Unlike balanced trees, tries don't depend on the number of stored keys, making them efficient for large datasets with long strings.

lessons.title: Suffix Trees and Suffix Arrays: Overview
lessons.content: Suffix trees and suffix arrays are advanced text data structures used for pattern matching, substring queries, and solving string problems efficiently. Suffix trees are compressed tries of all suffixes of a string, enabling fast substring queries. Suffix arrays are space-efficient alternatives supporting similar queries.

lessons.title: Applications of Tries and Text Data Structures
lessons.content: Tries are used in autocomplete, spell checkers, IP routing, and dictionary implementations. Suffix trees/arrays aid in bioinformatics for genome analysis, plagiarism detection, and string pattern matching.
